title: Logical closure: one r>=3 counterexample disproves contractibility in general

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body: **Gap E (logical closure).** State explicitly that the question 'Is $F_s$ contractible?' is universally quantified over all reducible quasi-reduced words $s$, so that a single counterexample answers it with **No**. Record that the witness $w=aa^{-1}bb^{-1}aa^{-1}cc^{-1}aa^{-1}$ requires $r\ge3$ (three distinct generators $a,b,c$). Since $F_w\cong S^2$, we have $\pi_2(F_w)=\mathbb{Z}\neq0$, so $F_w$ is not even 2-connected, a fortiori not contractible. Conclude the answer is No.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
## Mathematical Review (critic-agent)

I independently re-derived and **machine-verified the entire combinatorial skeleton** of the attempt and confirm the geometric gaps coincide with the six already-tracked issues G1-G6. Summary:

**Verified correct (no gap):**
- Crossing-count distribution over the 15 pairings of $P=\{1,2,5,6,9,10\}$: five with 0, six with 1, three with 2, one ($N=\{1,6\}\{2,9\}\{5,10\}$) with 3. So 5+6+3 admissible cells if $N$ is excluded.
- Edge endpoints (eq:edges) and square facets (eq:faces): every one of my computed resolutions matches the tables exactly.
- $\chi=5-6+3=2$; every 1-cell lies on exactly two 2-cells; $\mathbb{Z}/2$ Betti numbers $(b_0,b_1,b_2)=(1,0,1)$.
- Every vertex link $\Lambda(Q_i)$ is a single cycle (connected, all nodes degree 2): triangles at $Q_1,Q_4$, bigons at $Q_2,Q_3,Q_5$. Hence the manifold/closed-surface conclusion is internally consistent.
- `lem:forced` (inert arcs $\{3,4\},\{7,8\}$ forced), W1 (locality of smoothing), `lem:commute` (disjoint-support smoothings commute): all correct.

**Genuine gaps (all already tracked):**
- **G1 / prob-07-7 — Even enclosure.** The mod-2 count $\sum_\gamma c_\gamma$ even is asserted via a vague "ordered incidences" parenthetical; the lemma is invoked for corner-turning region-boundary components even though its hypothesis forbids arc-ends in the interior. Needs a clean Jordan-curve parity argument.
- **G2 / prob-07-8 — pairing determines isotopy class.** The existence/uniqueness "arcs in minimal position are unique up to isotopy" is the backbone of the census and of embeddedness, but is stated without proof.
- **G3 / prob-07-9 — innermost bigon.** "a crossing subdivides a bigon into smaller bigons" is false in general (can give triangles/exit). Fix: innermost *arc-bounded region* contradicting `lem:bigon`(i).
- **G4 / prob-07-10 — sign vs generator.** $j-i$ odd gives opposite **sign**, which forces $w_i=w_j^{-1}$ only when $i,j$ share a generator. True inside $P$ (all $a^{\pm1}$); a boundary component with one end in $P$ and one in $\{3,4,7,8\}$ would have opposite sign but different generator. The claimed "inert-arc shielding" is plausible but unproved.
- **G5 / prob-07-11 — W2 region merge.** `lem:splice` assumes the four sectors at $c$ lie in distinct regions; coincident cases $R_2=R_4$ or $R_1=R_3$ (which genuinely occur) are not handled and can change the merge combinatorics / create-destroy a boundary circle.
- **G6 / prob-07-12 — surface argument.** `prop:s2` is correct *given* each square boundary is an embedded 4-cycle, i.e. given G2; inherits the G2 gap (not an independent error).

**Verdict.** The answer **No** and $F_w\cong S^2$ are almost certainly correct (the entire combinatorics checks out). The remaining work is purely to make the six geometric foundations G1-G6 rigorous. Concrete fixes for each are in the attached Critic Analysis doc.

No new issues created (G1-G6 + census already cover every gap I found).
